name: MKI Media Hero
overview: A cinematic hero banner on the Jellyfin home screen.
description: Adds a full-width hero carousel to the Jellyfin home screen. The list is prepared on the server from recently added, top rated and (optionally) Seerr trending titles, filtered per library with title, genre, tag and rating whitelists and blacklists. Layout, transitions, text and buttons are configurable. Settings page is in German.

versions.changelog: Renamed to MKI Media Hero so all MKI plugins sit together in the plugin list. Settings are kept.
Jellyseerr is now Seerr: renamed the trending sources and all labels. Settings are kept.
Per-library targets, sources as upper limits, paged Jellyseerr trending lookup, browser caching and a background pre-warmer.

name: MKI Merge Versions
overview: Two resolutions, one entry. The 4K version leads.
description: Merges movies that exist in several resolutions into a single library entry, matched by TMDb ID (IMDb as fallback), never by title. The highest resolution becomes the primary version. Runs as a scheduled task and automatically once the library has been quiet for five minutes. Includes a dry-run mode. Settings page is in German.

versions.changelog: First release: links versions via the database, groups by TMDb/IMDb, highest resolution becomes primary, own settings page.

name: MKI Seerr Bridge
overview: Seerr inside Jellyfin: button, embedded view, search and sign-in.
description: Brings Seerr into the Jellyfin web client: a button in the header and side menu, Seerr embedded in Jellyfin instead of a redirect, Seerr suggestions under Jellyfin search results with one-click requests attributed to the right user, optional single sign-on via Quick Connect, and a compatibility bridge for clients that still send legacy X-Emby authorization headers. Settings page is in German; the button label follows each user's language.

versions.changelog: Renamed to MKI Seerr Bridge so all MKI plugins sit together in the plugin list. Settings are kept.
Renamed to Seerr Bridge: Jellyseerr is now Seerr. All labels, descriptions and the menu route (#/seerr) follow the new name. Settings are kept.
Header and side-menu button, embedded view, search suggestions with requests, single sign-on via Quick Connect, legacy auth header bridge.
